# RTR-RE mode (no MCP server)

Persistent project memory and context discipline, carried by this plugin
alone. Retrieval runs through the `rtr-cli` command when it is installed
(`uv tool install rtr-role-type-retrieval`, or `uvx rtr-role-type-retrieval`);
when it is absent, say so in one line and work from the files in front of
you. Never invent a memory result.

Off only via "stop rtr", "normal mode", or `/rtr off`; confirm in one line
and stop applying this ruleset for the session. A new session reactivates.
Plain `/rtr` confirms on in one line and continues the current task.

## The memory loop

- Session start: run `rtr-cli session-start <project>` and read what it
  restores before planning. Run `rtr-cli stats` when you need corpus size.
- Before repeating past work: `rtr-cli search "<query>" --k 3` (add
  `--project <name>` to scope, `--dense-only` to skip lexical reranking).
  Use `rtr-cli explain "<query>"` when a ranking looks wrong.
- When you learn something durable: `rtr-cli write <project> <filename>
  "<markdown>"`. One fact per entry, domain words, no session chatter.
- After adding or changing memory files outside the CLI:
  `rtr-cli index` (add `--force` only for a full rebuild).
- Session end: `rtr-cli session-commit <project>` reflects, materializes,
  links, and indexes in one step.
- Housekeeping when results smell stale: `rtr-cli janitor --dry-run`
  first, read the report, then run it for real only if the report is right.
- Compressor, direct: `rtr-cli symbiose-compress <project> <target>`
  fires to a verbatim tail with thinking intact; `rtr-cli symbiose-drain`
  `<project>` consumes keeper sidecars; `rtr-cli symbiose-submit` uses presets.

## Context budget

Keep verbatim until 400000 tokens (Re-Symbiose-Mugen, the shipped
default); above that, evict to a 200000-token preserved tail of at
most 200 messages. What leaves the window sinks to session files
verbatim and stays retrievable through search — evicted is never
deleted. Prefer a search over re-reading a long file you already
summarized this session.

## AUTO-OPTIMIZE

Between every file read and the next code write, run one optimize pass on
what you are about to write — unasked, every time, in this order. On
OpenCode the plugin instigates the pass after your first read of a
cycle; on Claude Code and Codex no hook instigates it yet, so run it
yourself from this checklist.

1. Reuse: a helper, pattern, or path already in what you read does part of
   this job. Use it instead of writing a second one.
2. Delete: a branch, parameter, or layer in your draft earns nothing.
   Remove it before it ships, not after review.
3. Simplify: the draft has a shorter form with the same behavior — fewer
   elements, clearer names, one purpose per function.
4. Outperform the first draft: name one concrete way the code you are
   about to write is better than the obvious first version (a case it
   handles, a test it makes possible, a failure it makes loud). If you
   cannot name one, look again at what you read.

The pass is a checklist you run, not a rewrite of code you have not read.
It never expands scope: optimize the change being made, name adjacent
opportunities in one line, and leave them for the operator to order.
Verify after writing: run the relevant test or command and read its exit
code directly. An optimization nobody measured is a guess.

## Honesty rules

- A search with no results is a result. Report it; do not fill the gap
  from general knowledge and call it memory.
- Every number you state about the corpus comes from `rtr-cli stats` or a
  file you read this session.
- If the CLI is missing, slow, or errors: print the error, fall back to
  direct file work, and say which parts of the loop were skipped.

# RTR-RE .mjs edition — persistent memory without an MCP server

Version 1.2.2. The full RTR-RE discipline for people who do not want to
run an MCP server: session memory, context budget rules, and **AUTO-OPTIMIZE** —
an optimize pass instigated between every file read and the next code
write, unasked, so code written by a model that never looks back still
gets a second look before it lands.

Retrieval itself runs through the `rtr-cli` command from the Python
package (`uv tool install rtr-role-type-retrieval`). The plugin starts
no server, opens no socket, and holds no index: it injects the rules,
keeps the mode on, and points the agent at the CLI. If `rtr-cli` is
missing, the rules say so out loud and the session continues on files.

## Install (OpenCode)

The npm installer route (terminal-native, no browser, no network):

```bash
npx rtr-re-installer
```

Manual: copy `mjs/.opencode/` into your project or `~/.config/opencode/`
(plugins in those directories load automatically), plus `mjs/hooks/`,
`mjs/skills/`, and `mjs/AGENTS.md` beside them at the same relative
paths the core expects — or clone this repo and add to `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugin": ["@saimonokuma/rtr-re-mjs"] }
```

## Install (Claude Code / Codex)

Wire `hooks/claude-codex-hooks.json` as your hooks file (or merge its
three events): SessionStart injects the full ruleset, UserPromptSubmit
keeps a one-line reminder alive and catches the toggles, SubagentStart
covers delegated work.

## Toggles

On by default every new session. Off for the session only:
`/rtr off`, `stop rtr`, or `normal mode`. Back on: `/rtr` or `/rtr on`.
The off state is one flag file (`.rtr-off` in the host config dir);
deleting it turns the mode back on.

## AUTO-OPTIMIZE, exactly

State machine in `hooks/rtr-core.js` (`createAutoOptimizer`): the first
`read` tool result of a cycle gets one appended line — reuse what you
read, delete what earns nothing, simplify, name one concrete way the
draft beats the obvious first version. Further reads stay silent; the
next `write`/`edit` re-arms. The plugin never edits code itself; it
instigates the agent at the moment the draft forms.

## Parity with the MCP server (32 tools), honestly

| Surface | .mjs edition |
|---|---|
| search, explain, write, index, stats, init, consolidate, session-start, session-commit, reflect, materialize, update-graph, lexikon (add/show/build), janitor (16) | `rtr-cli` bridge — same engine, same index |
| context_plan | native JS arithmetic (`planContext`, same defaults) |
| keeper window discipline | rules + budget numbers in the ruleset; the native keeper plugin (`opencode-plugin/rtr-re-keeper.js`) remains the enforcement arm |
| discover, list, inbox, organize, delete, rtr_status, symbiose submit/poll | not on the CLI today: rules degrade to direct file work + `session-commit`; named as the next CLI slice, not faked |

## Architecture (one core, three shells)

`hooks/rtr-core.js` (zero dependencies) owns state, the rules cascade
(SKILL.md → AGENTS.md → inline fallback), toggles, AUTO-OPTIMIZE,
context-plan arithmetic, CLI argument building, and per-host hook
output. `.opencode/plugins/rtr.mjs` is the thin OpenCode shell over
that same core (`createRequire`), so no rule exists in two places.
`AGENTS.md` is generated from `skills/rtr/SKILL.md` by
`scripts/generate-agents.js`; the test suite fails if they drift.

Tests: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (also `npm test`).

## 🧪 Evaluation

The no-MCP edition shares the engine, the index, and the numbers: rtr-full
leads combined (R@1 0.723, R@3 0.850, MRR 0.777, 898 queries, 0 errors).
Install via npm, measure via pypi (`rtr-cli`), source on git.

| Taxon | What it isolates |
|---|---|
| T1–T6 | title, rare-term, concept, scoped, paraphrase, ident |
| T7–T12 | DTD structural + family discrimination |
| T13 keeper-memory | evicted-span retrievability (0.975) |

description: Turn rtr-re off for this session, or confirm it is on
---

If $ARGUMENTS is off (or "stop rtr" / "normal mode"): say so in one line and stop applying this ruleset for the rest of the session.

If $ARGUMENTS is empty or on: confirm rtr-re is on in one line, then carry on with whatever was being discussed.

If $ARGUMENTS names a memory action (search, stats, index, write, session-start, session-commit, janitor, explain, symbiose-submit, symbiose-drain, symbiose-compress): run it through rtr-cli and report the measured result, or say in one line that rtr-cli is not installed.
